title: Introduction to the Indian Stock Market: NSE, BSE, and SEBI
content:
The Indian stock market is one of the fastest-growing and most dynamic financial ecosystems in the world. It provides a transparent platform for corporate enterprises to raise public capital and for individual retail investors to participate in India's long-term economic expansion.

At the core of the Indian equity market are two premier national stock exchanges:
1. National Stock Exchange (NSE): Established in 1992, the NSE is the largest financial exchange in India by trading volume and market capitalization. Its flagship benchmark index is the Nifty 50, which tracks the performance of 50 top blue-chip companies across key sectors.
2. Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE): Established in 1875 on Dalal Street in Mumbai, the BSE is Asia's oldest stock exchange. Its marquee benchmark index is the S&P BSE Sensex, tracking 30 well-established corporations.

To begin investing in Indian equities, an investor needs a 'Three-in-One' account structure consisting of a Bank Account, a Trading Account, and a Demat Account. The Demat (Dematerialized) account acts as a digital locker that securely holds shares and securities in electronic form, maintained by registered depositories—either NSDL (National Securities Depository Limited) or CDSL (Central Depository Services Limited). Discount brokers such as Zerodha, Groww, and Angel One facilitate retail access through user-friendly mobile and web platforms.

The entire Indian capital market is strictly supervised and regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Established under the SEBI Act of 1992, SEBI's primary mandate is protecting retail investor interests, enforcing market transparency, and preventing insider trading and financial fraud.
